missionPremise: Card ZONING-BAND1 (F-01, dispatch _dispatches/2026-09-01_zoning-band1_dispatch.md): eight cities (Smithville, Luling, Martindale, Woodcreek, Lakeway, Robinson, Leander, Taylor) already have staged public zoning GIS layers per the ZONING-INGEST measurement (blocker B1: stamp CLI + ZONING_LAYERS live in legacy-design-tools, not hauska-engine) and are unstamped or partly stamped -- a stamp gap, not an acquire gap. No acquisition authorized or performed.
completionPredicate: Per city: before/after stamp counts, a named sample parcel verified against the correct jurisdiction, and an honest statement of whether the parcel's district reaches a real codified setback rule or honest-declines. Robinson's named Waco-bleed fixed for the resolvable subset. Bake-cost question (B2) answered with the correct county count. Met below for all eight cities.
scopeBasis: Scoped to the eight named cities and the LDT repo only, per the dispatch's explicit do-not list (no acquisition, no re-acquiring the five already-wired cities, no Bastrop-city setback rules applied elsewhere, no placeholder counted as a value, no bleed fix outside this card's cities, no setback-rule atoms minted, no repo touched besides the registered LDT worktree). hauska-engine was read-only referenced (already-open worktree from prior context) purely to understand the separate atom-store setback path the dispatch's 188,103-placeholder figure describes; nothing was written there.
whatContradictedTheCard: Two real contradictions, both verified at source rather than assumed: (1) the card states the eight cities span 'four counties' -- they actually span SIX distinct county FIPS (Bastrop 48021, Caldwell 48055, Hays 48209, Travis 48453, McLennan 48309, Williamson 48491), confirmed by reading every city's countyFips in ZONING_LAYERS. (2) The card's premise table states Leander is already stamped '2,150 of 26,587' and Taylor '2,576 of 8,541'. Direct, scoped, exit-code-confirmed queries against the live production store showed ZERO zoning_jurisdiction stamps anywhere in Williamson county before this card ran -- not just Leander/Taylor, but also the long-established Georgetown (whose own file header claims 'verified live 2026-07-20') and Round Rock. A related, non-contradicting finding: 130,766 Williamson-county rows DO carry a zoning_district value with zoning_jurisdiction left NULL, consistent with those four cities having been stamped by an EARLIER version of the write path that predates the zoning_jurisdiction column ever being populated -- explaining why a plausible-sounding premise number existed at all, without confirming it. Separately (not a contradiction, a process gap found and fixed): the worktree this card inherited from a lane the operator killed mid-work on 2026-09-01 was never registered in _catalog/seat_register.json, and the SEAT-01 hook correctly refused the first commit attempt until it was registered.

robinson-tx.bleedFix: 15 McLennan parcels flipped from waco-tx to robinson-tx (waco-tx county total 48,686 -> 48,671). 5,380 of the 5,796 robinson-tx parcels carry a 'WACO, TX 76706' postal address -- Robinson shares Waco's zip/postal-city designation despite being a separate incorporated city, which is almost certainly why the original Waco stamp bled here in the first place. Mechanism: whole-county overwrite-in-place UPDATE keyed by feature_index -- any parcel whose centroid matches BOTH Waco's and Robinson's polygons gets the later-run city (Robinson, run second). RESIDUAL NOT CLAIMED FIXED: a parcel genuinely inside Robinson's political limits but outside every polygon in Robinson's own 6,340-feature layer cannot be corrected by this mechanism and would remain waco-tx; no city-limits boundary table exists in this database to test that case independently (confirmed by table search), so this is named as an open risk, not verified absent.

bakeCostB2: CORRECTED: 8 cities span SIX counties, not four (see whatContradictedTheCard). Per B2, bake is a county-wide Factory publish, not city-scoped -- one-city bake still rewrites the county snapshot. So this card's work requires SIX separate county-wide bakes: Bastrop (63,357 total txgio_parcel rows), Caldwell (26,155 -- covers Luling AND Martindale in one bake, free batching since both share the county), Hays (117,427), McLennan (115,362), Williamson (304,298 -- covers Leander AND Taylor in one bake, same free batching), and Travis (828,773 -- by far the most expensive, roughly 7x the next-largest county and disproportionate to Lakeway's own 10,829-parcel share of it). Whether the publish JOB ITSELF can batch multiple counties per invocation was not verified in this card (hauska-factory is a different repo, out of scope) -- inferred from the single `--county=<fips>` argument shape of the factory-p2-juris job documented in 90_runbooks/seat_loop.md, stated here as an inference, not a source-verified fact. Recommendation, not an instruction: run the five small/medium counties first (Bastrop, Caldwell, Hays, McLennan, Williamson) and treat Travis as its own separately-scheduled, most-expensive bake given the size disparity -- but the actual publish trigger and cost model live in a repo this card was scoped out of.
setbackSummaryAcrossEight: Two systems exist and this close names both, per the card's own instinct not to leave 'which is authoritative' ambiguous: (1) LDT's own local, hand-curated JSON setback tables (lib/adapters/src/local/setbacks/), the only one this repo's buildable-envelope route actually consumes. Of the eight Band-1 cities, SIX (Smithville, Luling, Martindale, Woodcreek, Lakeway, Robinson) have NO entry here at all -- not a placeholder, an outright absence, which is a stronger and more honest signal than a placeholder table since the code path has nothing to fabricate from and correctly returns null. TWO (Leander, Taylor) have real, citation-backed tables with meaningful leading-token alignment to their zoning layers, detailed per-city above. (2) The separate atom-store setback-rule population (188,103 atoms, mostly placeholder under storage-port-proof/phase-1a per the dispatch) lives in hauska-engine/the Factory substrate and is consumed by a different product surface -- not read or written by this card, confirmed by reading (not writing to) that repo's detect-placeholder-setback-citation.mjs to understand its scope before concluding it was a separate system.

processFinding.seatRegisterGap: P:/tmp/legacy-design-tools-zoning-band1 (the worktree the 2026-09-01 killed lane left behind) was not in _catalog/seat_register.json. The SEAT-01 hook correctly refused the first commit attempt (UNREGISTERED_WORKTREE), and a second attempt registered with the shared-path pattern (path=P:/legacy-design-tools, matching the primary worktree) also correctly refused (PRODUCT_INDEX_FOREIGN) because ownerOfRepoPath() resolves to the FIRST-listed entry for a shared repoPath, which is always the primary. Fixed by registering self-contained (path=worktree), matching the pattern already in use by the concurrently-running hauska-engine-cell-ledger entry -- confirmed this is the correct pattern for a seat-loop queue-card lane (self-service commit per 90_runbooks/seat_loop.md) as opposed to a hand-carry lane (whose diff 'the planner commits' from the primary worktree, e.g. legacy-design-tools-p106). Worth a planner note: any future queue-card lane inheriting an ad hoc /tmp worktree from before the SEAT-01 hook armed will hit this same two-step failure unless it registers self-contained from the start.

fleetMemory: LESSON: this repo's real production DB secret for legacy-design-tools is DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL_DIRECT under GCP project legacy-design-tools-prod, NOT hauska-prod-497015 (where it does not exist). CORTEX_DATABASE_URL and SOURCE_DATABASE_URL under hauska-prod-497015 happen to reach the identical physical Neon database (cross-verified by write-under-one/read-under-other), so either works for this repo's data, but the deploy workflow and the Cloud Run service (cortex-api) both live under legacy-design-tools-prod, not hauska-prod-497015 -- 'gcloud run services list' against the wrong project silently returns zero matches rather than an error, which is exactly the kind of convenient-looking negative result ENFORCEMENT.md warns against trusting.

LESSON: zoning_jurisdiction can be NULL on a large population of parcels that DO have zoning_district set (130,766 in Williamson county alone) -- these predate the jurisdiction column's use and are invisible to any bleed/coverage check that filters on zoning_jurisdiction. A stamp-count premise sourced from zoning_district alone (or from some other proxy) can look like real jurisdiction-tagged coverage when it is not; verify against the actual column the downstream bleed logic reads, not a plausible-sounding adjacent one.

LESSON: a killed lane's worktree that predates the SEAT-01 hook needs registering self-contained (path=worktree) if the successor card intends to self-service-commit per seat_loop.md, not the shared-path pattern used by hand-carry lanes -- the two patterns are not interchangeable and the wrong one fails with a confusing PRODUCT_INDEX_FOREIGN rather than a clear 'wrong pattern' message.

GROUND-TRUTH (2026-09-02, verified live): Williamson county (48491) had zero zoning_jurisdiction-stamped parcels across ALL FOUR of its configured cities (Georgetown, Round Rock, Leander, Taylor) before this card, despite Georgetown's own file-header comment claiming live verification on 2026-07-20 -- the verification likely happened against zoning_district/a different check, not against jurisdiction-tagged coverage as this card measured it.
